- **Focus harness:** `Harness::focused()` / `hovered()`.
- **Keyboard harness:** a Tab and Shift+Tab key-press focus check exists on the stand, driven through the harness's `press` / `press_with` (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`); since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction a range-input key and click check runs in both layout modes (`range_input_interaction.rs`: a 7-row keys table and a 5-row clicks table, one `input` per change and none on a no-change Home, the input focused after every click, a disabled range taking neither keys nor a click), and on the stand `stand_act_range.rs` moves the Timer slider through the driver by click and key, an arrow step after two Tabs leaving it focused with role `Slider`, its name and the forward focus sequence unchanged; a select key and typeahead check runs in both layout modes — `select_interaction` (18 tests: a 14-row keys table and a 7-row typeahead table, one `input` and one `change` per change and none for no change, the typed text kept for one second of the document's clock, a disabled select taking no key and no click) and, through the driver, `stand_act_select` (10 tests: Tab `fx-before` → `fx-pick` → `fx-named` → `fx-after` → `fx-before`, the disabled `fx-off` skipped, an option chosen by a click then a key) — both in the `a11y` leg, both three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg, `stand_act_select` by its `stand_` prefix and `select_interaction` by the leg's named `--test` list; # Accessibility Rules

Path-scoped rules for the accessibility tree, keyboard/focus handling, painted colours and the stand.
Source: `.andromeda/a11y-plan.md` — tier 0, target SC 2.1.1 (keyboard) · 1.4.3 (contrast) · 2.4.3 (focus order). The reach is published in `docs/capabilities.md` under `## Accessibility reach` (tier 0, those three criteria and no other, the `a11y` leg's files, what an assistive technology reads unmeasured, the named limits — the focus fixup firing no `blur`, a single select's `size` unread, `aria-activedescendant` unread); its pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads none of these claims, so a change that moves the reach is made in that document by hand.

## Accessibility tree
- `build_accessibility_tree` returns an AccessKit `TreeUpdate`; the root is a `Window` node with id `u64::MAX`, the focused DOM node is tree focus only where it is among the built nodes, else `u64::MAX`, the window, so the tree never names a node it did not build, AccessKit ids are `NodeId::as_u64()`.
- Role = `role` attribute, else HTML-AAM element mapping, else `Role::Unknown`; only `<html>` and `<body>` should map to `Unknown` on a semantic page; an `img` whose `alt` is the empty string is decorative and reads the generic container role, not image (upstream's behaviour, `an_image_with_an_empty_alt_is_decorative` its pin). Known gap: strong native semantics can be overridden by `role` (contrary to WAI-ARIA 1.2).
- `hidden`, `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` exclude a node and its children — an `option` of a `select`, its child or under its `optgroup` (`is_select_option`), excepted from `display: none`, which every option of a single-choice select but its chosen one computes and a `multiple` select's rows do not: it stays in the tree, `hidden`, `inert` and `visibility: hidden` still excluding it; `aria-hidden="true"` keeps it, marked hidden; an element carrying `inert` is excluded with its children too, and so from the snapshot, and a hit passes through it, removing `inert` restoring the tree and the hit (the `inert` read ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).
- State = ARIA state attributes read by value on every element — a select's option excepted, its `selected` its chosen state (`select::is_chosen`), true or false, with no `aria-selected` read, and its non-empty `label` attribute its `label` where it has no `aria-label` —, the toggle by role (trimmed, lower-case, exact): `aria-selected` `true`/`false` → `selected`; `aria-pressed` `true`/`false`/`mixed` → `toggled` on every role but the five checkable ones; `aria-invalid` `true`/`grammar`/`spelling` → `invalid`, absent, empty or `false` → nothing, any other value → `Invalid::True`. `aria-checked` `true`/`false`/`mixed` → `toggled` on a `CheckBox` · `Switch` · `RadioButton` · `MenuItemCheckBox` · `MenuItemRadio` role alone (`role="switch"` mapping to `Switch`), a native `input` of type `checkbox` or `radio` reading neither attribute — the toggle read per role ratified by the founder (2026-10-18), `accessibility_states`' fourth test its pin; each attribute is read once, and the one other write of `toggled` is a native checkbox's or radio's own checked state on a checkable role — `Toggled::True` or `False` from `checkbox_input_checked()`; under any other role it writes nothing, so `pressed` never begins to read on it, `accessibility_states`' `a_click_and_a_space_move_a_native_control_in_the_tree` its pin, what an assistive technology reads of it not measured. A Dioxus `bool` attribute arrives as the text `"false"`, so state the literal texts `"true"` and `"false"`: a presence read would read every control pressed. `accessibility_states`, `inert_subtree` and `accessibility_active_descendant_unread`, outside the `stand_` prefix, also run three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg by its fixed `--test` list, each keeping its name, and in this leg too — as `select_interaction` (by that list) and `stand_act_select` (by its `stand_` prefix) are, so each runs in both the `a11y` and `stand-repeat` legs, as `stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast` and `stand_accessibility_ids` do. `select_popup`, `select_popup_painted` and `stand_act_popup` run in the workspace `test` leg and three `stand-repeat` rounds, the first two by its named `--test` list and `stand_act_popup` by its `stand_*` glob; # seven_guis (the stand)

_Crate notes. Primary sources: `doc:architecture` §Existing Scopes, `doc:layout-templates` desktop-native, the active `escher-X.Y.Z/intent.md`._

## Responsibility
The 7GUIs benchmark app ("Seven benchmark tasks for GUI frameworks") in Dioxus — tasks counter, temp_converter, flight_booker, timer, crud, circle_drawer, cells. escher's internal stand: every 0.1.0 capability (stable ids, snapshot, driver, screenshots, a11y) is proven on it headlessly, with a minimal fixture beside it where the tasks lack a case (an element covered by another is one).

## Key integrations

### Consumes from
- escher-driver (native target only): the second binary, `escher-session <verb> [arguments] --session <dir>` (`src/session_host.rs`), is the driver's command line over six served tasks — the four lean ones, Cells and the load page — and the one place a served task, the stand's boot and the timer's tick handle meet a driver `Session` — `main` installs the telemetry sink first, then hands argv, the six slugs `counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load` (a private `TASKS` table, from which the usage line's `apps:` and the MCP `start` tool's `enum` are written) and the stand's boot to `escher_driver::command_line`; the boot starts a session through `stand` only (Cells through `stand::boot_cells`, the load page through `stand::boot_load`) and hands the timer's session its time step (`stand::timer_step` over the tick handle, through `Session::with_time`; the other five carry none and still take `advance`, which moves their session's clock alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)). `start <task> [--record <dir>]` checks its recording directory itself before it spawns, then spawns the same binary in its host role, `serve <task> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]` (passing `--record` to the host); since 2026-10-19-session-recording `--record <dir>`, taken at most once on `start`, the host role and the `mcp` role, keeps the session as one owner-only replayable check — `check-{n}.json` (`0600`, never replacing a file) in a `0700` directory whose parent must exist, removed by escher only when its recording fails, holding per call its verb, arguments, acceptance, the answer's digest and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, the answer itself as an `answer` key — the line the driver wrote, masked as on every carrier, a shot's kept as `{"width":…,"height":…}` without its `png` — read back and replayed by `Check::replay` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19: F1 A · F2 B, F3 B) — a directory open to its group or others refused as the session error `record-dir-not-private` (exit 3, `start` spawning nothing), a recording that ends answering `recording-failed` (exit 3; over MCP `isError`); the host serves until `stop` or its 30-minute idle expiry and writes nothing to stdout; every other command is one client run that answers one line of JSON on stdout (exit `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error — the four read from `EXIT_STATUSES` and served by `help`), save `help` (since 2026-10-12-self-description), which needs no `--session` — it admits at most one and reads it not — and answers the tool's self-description with status `0`, reaching no session; the `mcp` role lists it as its fifteenth tool, last, `graph` after `lint`, `actions` after `graph` and `layout` after `actions`. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the seventh instance verb, `screenshot [--id <id>] --session <dir>`, answers one uncoloured line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` on stdout, exit 0 — the whole screen, or with `--id` the element cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — an app with no font it can paint text with refused `fonts-unavailable` and an element shot that crops to no pixel `off-screen`, exit 1; over the `mcp` role an accepted shot is an `image` block (`image/png`, base64) then a text block, the line without `png`. The eighth instance verb, `lint --session <dir>`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"findings":[…]}` on stdout, exit 0, each finding keyed `id` · `defect` · `bounds` then its reason's keys — ids, closed words and numbers only — an app with no font it can paint text with refused `fonts-unavailable`, exit 1, a `lint` step kept under `--record` like every instance verb; over the `mcp` role an accepted `lint` answers its JSON line of findings as one text block. The ninth instance verb, `graph --session <dir>`, after `lint`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}` on stdout, exit 0, carrying ids, component names, handler event names, registered state names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value; over the `mcp` role an accepted `graph` answers its JSON line `{"nodes","states"}` as one text block. The tenth instance verb, `actions --session <dir>`, after `graph`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"nodes":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"keyed":…,"verbs":[{"verb":…,"cause":…}]}]}` on stdout, exit 0, `owner` and `cause` left out when absent, carrying ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, closed cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`, the answer unpaged; over the `mcp` role an accepted `actions` answers its JSON line `{"nodes"}` as one text block. The eleventh instance verb, `layout --id <id> --session <dir>`, after `actions`, takes one required `--id` and answers one uncoloured line of `id`, `bounds`, `laid_out`, `placed`, `shifts`, `width` and `height` on stdout, exit 0 — where the element sits and why at its size, ids, closed words and numbers only, changing nothing — kept under `--record` like every instance verb. The first instance verb, `snapshot [--part <part>] --session <dir>`, takes an optional `--part` (a whole number, 1 to 1000) and answers one uncoloured line on stdout, exit 0 — `{"text":…}` for a whole screen, `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}` for a screen read in parts, from part 1 without `--part`, a part past the last the empty text with the same `parts`, a `--part` outside its bound refused `malformed`, exit 1; over the `mcp` role a paged `snapshot` answers its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` as one text block, a whole screen still the bare screen text. The former two-argument form `<task> <state-dir>` is gone. A fourth role, `escher-session coverage <app> <check>...` — one app the binary boots, then one or more kept-check paths, no `--session` and no `--record` word among them, any other shape usage (stderr, exit 2) — reads each path bounded at `MAX_CHECK_BYTES + 1` and parses it by `Check::from_bytes` (unreadable, past the bound, no check or a check of another app refused `malformed`, exit 1), replays each check on a fresh boot through the same boot `main` hands to the command line and answers one uncoloured line `{"unexercised":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"event":…}],"checks":n,"held":m}` on stdout, exit 0, `owner` left out when absent; a boot that fails ends with the session error, exit 3. Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface its `mcp` role, `escher-session mcp [--record <dir>]` (the `--record` since 2026-10-19-session-recording), is an MCP server over its standard streams (`escher_driver::serve_mcp`): its `start` tool, its `enum` naming the six, boots one of the six served tasks through the same boot and holds it in process, adding no markup; it writes protocol lines only on stdout and ends with nothing there. Eight test targets spawn it, sharing `tests/common/mod.rs` (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface also `Speaker`, a child spoken to over piped stdin under a 30 s reply bound, and, stated once for the two log checks `host_log` and `mcp_log` alone, what they read stderr with: `Needles` and `stand_needles` (the CRUD stand's id and name needles, booted in process through `stand::boot`), `stamped_lines`, `found`, `occurrences`, `option_needles` (the needles of a select's options), the unix-only `recorded_needles`, `graph_needles` (each served component and registered state name, for the one `graph` call each log check makes, read 0 times on stderr), `actions_needles` (the CRUD screen's listed author-key ids holding a `-`, for the one `actions` call each log check makes, read 0 times on stderr) and `cells_needles(part)` (part `part`'s author keys of the in-process Cells screen, booted through `stand::boot_cells`, and the middle column-A cell it holds, for `host_log`'s Cells part read)): `tests/host_binary.rs` is the host role's smoke (on `counter`); `tests/host_log.rs` checks that at `RUST_LOG=trace` a host running three calls writes one command-span line per call and no stable id, no accessible name and no typed text to stderr (on `crud`, per package and under the workspace build, and on `cells`, its paged part read — a sentinel committed into a part-2 cell, then `snapshot --part 2`, in `hl-cells`, and for a select's list opened and chosen through the host, in `hl-popup`), and its unix-only recording-clients check runs the binary as a client — `start crud --record` through `stop`, each run at `RUST_LOG=trace`, in `hl-client` and `hl-client-rec`, a `Started` guard stopping the session; `tests/host_timer.rs` boots the timer host and moves it by a hosted `advance`; `tests/cli_commands.rs` runs every driver command as a process on the four tasks and, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, pins that a write to a closed stdout is dropped (`a_closed_stdout_drops_the_answer_and_keeps_the_ending`: `help` exits 0 and `snapshot` with no session 3, neither printing a panic); `tests/cli_flow.rs` runs the two POSIX `sh` flows of `tests/flows/` (`counter.sh`, `flight.sh`); `tests/mcp_server.rs` drives the `mcp` role through the Counter flow by tool calls alone and its protocol errors, and compares a snapshot with the command line's and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`'s bytes with the command line's (those two tests unix only), and speaks the newest revision with `help` answered before any `start`; `tests/mcp_log.rs` reads the role at `RUST_LOG=trace` — no id, no name, no typed text, one `tool_call` line per call — per package and under the workspace build; the two MCP targets run on windows too; since 2026-10-19-session-recording `tests/recording.rs` spawns both the host role and the `mcp` role, with `--record`, and runs `tests/flows/record_checks.sh` — the third POSIX `sh` script of `tests/flows/`, no test target — under `sh` into `rc-fresh` (under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`), comparing both recorded files byte for byte with the two committed checks `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json` (git mode `100644`, the one exception to a kept check's owner-only medium; no `screenshot` step, a shot's PNG bytes differing by OS). Since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the cold-agent pipe (`scripts/cold-agent.sh run`) gives its `claude` client this binary's `mcp` role as its one MCP server, `escher` (`target/debug/escher-session mcp --record target/cold-agent/record`, the owner-only record directory `run` makes and `cleanup` removes, its kept checks never printed, spawned through the per-run `mcp.json`, `RUST_LOG=info`, stderr to `target/cold-agent/server.log`), and its judge spawns two more `escher-session mcp` children, without `--record`, to replay the agent's check, full and ablated; the pipe builds nothing — a missing or non-executable binary is exit 3 naming `cargo build --locked -p seven_guis --bin escher-session`. Since 2026-10-14-quality-gates the `stand-repeat` CI leg runs these eight by name (`cargo test -p seven_guis --locked` over `cli_commands`, `cli_flow`, `host_binary`, `host_log`, `host_timer`, `mcp_server`, `mcp_log` and `recording`) in each of its three rounds — a zero-failure budget, no retry.
- dioxus-native (native binary `seven_guis_native`) or a wasm32 cdylib (`--no-default-features --features vello-gpu`, `console_error_panic_hook`).
- escher-telemetry (native target only): `main` calls `escher_telemetry::init(escher_telemetry::service_identity!())` before `launch` — stderr log lines carry `service.name=seven_guis`; an init `Err` is `eprintln!`ed and the stand still launches. The engine `tracing` features stay off in a `-p seven_guis` build; a workspace-wide build turns blitz-dom's on, and with it blitz-dom's `writing-mode`, which selects the body of the bounds reader that every snapshot `bounds` and `visible_region` read through (test-plan §9 → Engine features by runner).

- On the native target only, escher-telemetry, blitz-test-harness and blitz-traits (the headless stand) and escher-driver (the session its `escher-session` binary hosts), with `dioxus-native` features `system-fonts` + `woff` — `woff` decodes the bundled DejaVu woff2 in every build that includes the stand. seven_guis is a `[workspace.dependencies]` path entry with default features (dioxus-native refuses to compile with no renderer); blitz-tests consumes it as a dev-dependency.

### Publishes to
- Screens: Home (centered 640px column of task cards with description and tag, inside a box that scrolls — at the stand's 800 × 600 viewport that box is 600 high and the seventh card, Cells, lies below it until scrolled into view) and TaskShell (header with back button, title, spacer over a scrolling body); headless only, two screens beside the lean four, each by a boot of its own — Cells (`boot_cells`) and the load page (`boot_load`: TaskShell titled "Load" over the button `load-fetch` "Load", white on `#3a5ce5`, hover `#2a4cd3`, active `#1f3fc1`, and the paragraph `load-done` "Loaded", `display: none` until the stylesheet the click links lands, no CSS selecting by id).
- The headless stand `seven_guis::stand` (native only): `LeanTask { Counter, FlightBooker, Timer, Crud }`; pinned `VIEWPORT_WIDTH 800` · `VIEWPORT_HEIGHT 600` · `HIDPI_SCALE 1.0` · `COLOR_SCHEME Light`; `font_ctx()` (bundled DejaVu Sans, the one font, system fonts off — every generic family and any unavailable named family lays out in it by fallback, guarded by `stand_bundled_font_families`); `options(incremental) -> HarnessOptions` (offline: `net_provider: None`); `boot(LeanTask, options) -> Harness<DioxusDocument>` and `boot_timer(options) -> (Harness, TimerTicks)` — each a fresh `VirtualDom` mounting the task in TaskShell (no Home) with a no-op Back; `boot_cells(options)`, Cells in TaskShell, no `LeanTask`, its screen past the snapshot text's budget and read in parts; `boot_load(options)`, the load page in TaskShell, its `net_provider` replaced by the private `LoadNet` — each `fetch` answering the fixed `LOADED_CSS` for the fixed `LOAD_URL` `http://stand.test/load.css` from a thread of its own after `LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY` (200 ms), no `is_noop` override, so the harness counts its load — every other boot offline; `TIMER_TICK_MS` (100) and `timer_step(TimerTicks)`, the Timer's time step for a driver session (`Session::with_time`): it delivers the whole ticks the milliseconds asked hold, carrying the remainder below one tick across calls (250 then 250 deliver 2 then 3 ticks), and returns nothing — the session, not the step, moves the harness's clock (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18). `start_in`, a lean task started in a named fixture state, refuses a name outside its task's closed fixture table before anything boots — Crud holds `fourteen-people` and `person-selected`, Flight Booker `return-flight`, Counter and Timer none; the state is reached in process through `Session::reach` (each acting step a validated call, stopping at the first refused or unsettled step with the earlier steps standing), a recorded session keeping the reach's steps as ordinary calls so its check replays from boot, and no fixture state rides the driver's carriers (command line, MCP, session socket, kept check). The stand also boots one component alone, in the same pinned 800 × 600 Light viewport with the one bundled font; no driver carrier reaches a component alone (no verb, argument, MCP tool, socket call or kept check). It installs no telemetry, reads no env var, names no `blitz_net`.
- `app::Task` (pub) and `app::task_in_shell(Task, EventHandler<()>)` — the windowed `app()` and the stand render through the same mapping; `pub fn TaskShell` — the shell a test-local variant of a task mounts in so its unkeyed ids read as the task's. `DEJAVU_SANS` — the crate-root woff2 bytes, shared by the wasm entry and the stand. `tasks::use_graph_signal(name, writers, init) -> Signal<T>` — `use_signal` with `use_graph_state`, through which every task's signals register (the stand shell's `active` and `stand.rs`'s `linked` stay `use_signal`); its writers a `&'static [DeclaredWrite]` built from the `const fn` `tasks::writes(id, event)`, written `const { &[…] }` or as a `const` item, a bare `&[writes(..)]` erroring `E0716`.
- `tasks::timer::TimerTicks` — the timer's tick seam: absent from context, the timer runs its 100 ms `futures_timer::Delay`; present, each `deliver(n)` tick is one 0.1 s step capped at the duration, applied on the next pass — a pump, an input helper's own pump, or a settle (`Harness::settle`, `Session::act`, each acting verb of `Session::run`), so a delivery made after an input helper waits for a later pass. Every stand boot provides one, so an undriven timer holds 0.0 s.

## Internal conventions
- Example CSS in `const CSS: &str` raw strings; accent `#3a5ce5` on `#f5f5f5` (one step darker since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions, `#4a6cf7` until then; white button text on it 5.47), text `#1a1a1a`; invalid `#e53e3e` family, success `#ebf8ee` family.
- Inputs replace the focus outline with a border colour or box-shadow on focus.
- `idna_adapter = "=1.0.0"` pin disables unicode URL support. A file that glob-imports the dioxus_native prelude spells a two-parameter result `std::result::Result` — on Android the glob brings manganis's one-parameter `Result` alias, a failure only the CI Android job sees.

## Stand-relevant behaviour
- Flight booker validates `dd.mm.yyyy` with month range and leap years; return not before start; invalid dates get an `invalid` class and disable Book.
- Two states are stated in markup, by attribute alone (2026-10-10-snapshot-states; no element, class, style, key, id or order moved): the flight booker's date inputs `flight-start` / `flight-return-date` state `aria-invalid`, `crud-list` is a `listbox` and each CRUD row an `option` with `aria-selected` — always the literal texts `"true"` and `"false"`. A snapshot reads them as `invalid` and `selected`. The stand states no `aria-pressed`: the flight booker's mode is one `select#flight-type` (class `type-select`, named by `aria-label` "Flight type" alone) holding `option#flight-type-one-way` (value `one-way`) and `option#flight-type-return` (value `return`), each `selected` from the `flight_type` signal — the snapshot reading it at boot `ComboBox "Flight type"` with value `one-way` and two `ListBoxOption`s, each at the select's client rect. A click, Enter, or a Space with no typed text standing opens `select#flight-type`'s list, the engine's select list in every document; focus stays on the select and the Tab sequence holds with the list open and after each close, Tab choosing the current row and closing before focus moves; while it is open each row reads its own `bounds` in the snapshot and the diff, the highlight in neither the snapshot nor the tree, and after a close the rows read back at the select's client rect; no stand markup, id, class or style moved. Since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness the CRUD list is a keyboard region — `crud-list` takes `tabindex="0"` and an `onkeydown`: ArrowDown selects the next visible row (the first when none is selected), ArrowUp the previous, Home the first and End the last, each filling `crud-name` and `crud-surname` as a row's click does, a key at the list's end or ArrowUp with no row selected changing nothing — so CRUD's Tab sequence reads `back-btn` · `crud-filter` · `crud-list` · `crud-name` · `crud-surname` · `crud-create` (six stops); no element, class, style, wrapper or row added, and the tree's focus is the list, never the row (no `aria-activedescendant` read). Since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions the list is named by an attribute alone — `aria-label="People"`, its accessible name `People` in the tree and the snapshot — adding no element, class, style, wrapper, id or order. Cells states no selected cell; stating it (`aria-selected` under a grid role) is owned by residual `res-wvatzhpe` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next) on the operator's "Key all three; C8 deferred" (2026-10-14).
- Cells: it calls its `MountedData` handles synchronously, kept since the bridge's buffered render though the hazard no longer needs it — a signal-writing task spawned from a key handler now reaches the document through `MountedData` with no `RefCell already borrowed` panic; tokenizer rejects unknown characters, reference cycles read `#CYCLE`, division by zero is an error; commits on Enter or blur. Since 2026-10-31-engine-debts `cells-grid` is a keyboard region and one Tab stop — `id`, `tabindex` 0, `aria_label` Cells and an `onkeydown`, with no role: arrows move `current`, clamped, into view through a synchronous `MountedData::scroll_to(ScrollBehavior::Instant)`, one `onmounted` per data cell holding the handles; Enter opens the editor on `current`, focused, and its Enter commits, stops propagation and returns focus to the grid; a click inside an open editor returns early and keeps its typed text; `.cells-grid:focus .cell.current` draws the accent outline, `2px solid #3a5ce5`; the Tab sequence is the one `CELLS_TAB_ORDER` states.
- Circle drawer clamps diameter 5–100.

## Entry points for modification
- `examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs` (Home, TaskShell, `task_in_shell`) · `src/stand.rs` (headless stand) · `src/tasks/*.rs` · `src/main.rs` · `src/lib.rs` (`DEJAVU_SANS`, wasm entry)

## Testing this crate
- Stand checks live in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_{boot,counter,flight_booker,timer,crud,element_ids,id_persistence,accessibility_ids,snapshot,snapshot_state,snapshot_text,diff,id_edits,actionable_keys}.rs`, each building its harness through `stand::boot` (or `Harness::from_vdom` with `stand::options` — for a fixture page through the shared `fixtures::boot` of `tests/fixtures/mod.rs` — for Home, the edit fixtures, the state fixture — a checkbox, two radios and a password input the lean tasks lack — the text check's two fixtures, a password input and a file input, and the diff check's three — a panel hidden by attribute, a password input and a label a button rewrites) and driving it with the harness input helpers: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --test stand_boot` (etc.). They assert unconditionally under the bundled font — no font skip, no sleep, no `dispatch_recorded`. Since 2026-10-14-quality-gates the `stand-repeat` CI leg (not a fast leg) runs every `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs`, one `--test` each, and, on the same line, seventeen named blitz-tests targets outside that prefix as literal `--test` words (`stand_requirement_sweep`'s `STAND_REPEAT_NAMED` still holding the first ten), each file keeping its name, in three rounds — a zero-failure budget, no retry, no `--ignored`. Each lean task's controls and value displays carry author `id`s (`counter-value`, `flight-book`, `timer-reset`, `crud-delete` …) that are their stable element ids — select them by `#id`; the pre-id checks still select by class and by structural selectors under `.crud-root`. Each CRUD row carries the Dioxus key `{person.id}`, its person's model-assigned `u64`, set on the `for` item itself with the filter in the iterator (a `key:` inside an `if` within the `for` would not key the list), and beside it the author `id` `crud-person-{person.id}` — so a row's id is `crud-person-0` · `-1` · `-2` on the fixture, Create from `crud-person-3`, and follows its person under filter, Create and Delete. Home's seven task cards carry `task-card-{slug}` (`counter`, `temp-converter`, `flight-booker`, `timer`, `crud`, `circle-drawer`, `cells`) — open a task with `#task-card-timer`. Every element an agent can act on must read an author key: `stand_actionable_keys` asserts `unkeyed_actionable()` empty on the four lean tasks and Home, so a new control there needs an `id`; since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep the temp converter, circle drawer and cells read it empty too (2 · 3 · 676 until then), Circle Drawer's dialog open included — keyed by author ids added as `id:` lines alone, no element, class, style, wrapper or order moving: `temp-celsius` · `temp-fahrenheit`; `circle-undo` · `circle-redo` · `circle-canvas` and, only while its dialog is open, `circle-diameter` (the dialog's range input) · `circle-close`; `cell-{A..Z}{0..25}` on the 676 data cells through the file's own `col_label(c)` and `cell-input` on the one edit input and, beside those, `cells-grid` on the grid, focusable and carrying a listener, so it reads its key (`stand_non_lean_tasks` reads it). The six task inputs are named by attributes alone — `r#for` on the existing labels of `timer-duration` / `crud-filter` / `crud-name` / `crud-surname`, `aria_label` on `flight-start` ("Departure date") and `flight-return-date` ("Return date"). seven_guis takes dioxus-native with no `accessibility` feature, so `just seven_guis` builds no AccessKit adapter; since 2026-10-07-act-by-id it gets dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` through its `escher-driver` edge, so both its binaries compile the `accessibility_tree` override and the snapshot modules — still with no adapter to hand a tree to. ## Harness contract (§3)

- **Test runner:** Rust built-in harness (`#[test]`, `#[tokio::test]`); `test-that` matchers in some tests; WPT runner for conformance; `unittest` for CI scripts.
- **In-process harness (measured):** `blitz-test-harness::Harness` — construct (`from_html`, `from_component`, `from_component_alone(component, props maker, options)` — one component mounted as the one child of an anonymous root, its props a maker run once in that root's scope, riding `from_vdom` and adding no carrier, `vdom_alone` its public mount, on which a caller provides a root context before the harness builds —, `from_vdom` — which, before its one pump, provides `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` as a root context where the vdom's root holds none, a root context the builder gave standing; `HarnessOptions` also takes `font_ctx` and `incremental`), `pump`/`tick`/`advance_time` (the harness's time a `VirtualClock` its harness-built documents read — `tick(dt)` advancing it, a negative or non-finite `dt` moving nothing, `advance_time(Duration)` by exactly the duration, each then pumping; `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never moving it; `wrap(doc)` keeping the clock the document's own config gave it; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), `settle` (that pass repeated until no work is due: `Settled`, or `NotSettled` naming the busy class — `Loads` at once when a request is in flight or a render-blocking resource is pending after a quiet pass, else `Render`, `Loads` or `Layout` read off the last pass at the 64-pass bound; no clock read but the harness's, no time advanced, no load waited on; the crate-private load counter forwarding `NetHandler::error` to the handler it wraps, so a failed stylesheet reaches the document, stops counting as a pending render-blocking resource and does not read `NotSettled { busy: Loads }`, and the driver's `settle_waiting` returns where it would otherwise have run to `LOAD_WAIT`), input helpers that pump, inspection (`query`, `layout_rect`, `text_content`, `focused`, `hit`, `dom_string`), and since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a paint with no display — `screenshot` / `screenshot_rect` into `VelloCpuImageRenderer`, composited over opaque white, at the harness's own time with no tick or pump, a document with no font refused `FontsUnavailable`; and since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness a contrast reader — `text_contrast(node_id) -> Option<TextContrast>`, reading and changing nothing (no mutation, input, pump or settle): the text-bearing element's computed `color`, font size and weight over the background composited source-over from its ancestors' `background-color`s onto the root-else-`body` canvas over opaque white, `None` with no text or where an element on the walk has `opacity` below 1, a filter, a background image or a `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal` (`paints_more_than_colour`, through `resolved_style_value`), `Session::lint`'s `contrast` reading the same with no second formula, and `contrast_ratio` the WCAG 2.x ratio. See `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`.
- **Headless stand (measured):** `seven_guis::stand::boot(LeanTask, options)` / `boot_timer(options)` mount counter, flight booker, timer or CRUD in TaskShell, and beside them `stand::boot_alone(component, props maker, options)` boots a component alone at the stand's viewport and font, `TimerTicks` provided on the root before the build, `stand::boot_cells(options)` boots Cells and `stand::boot_load(options)` the load page (TaskShell titled "Load"), read by the served-page checks and by `escher-session`'s six tasks — fresh `VirtualDom` per boot, pinned 800×600 · scale 1 · Light, bundled DejaVu Sans with system fonts off, offline (`net_provider: None` — every boot but `stand::boot_load`, which replaces it with the stand's `LoadNet`, answering `http://stand.test/load.css` from a thread of its own after 200 ms, and the error-text check's failing page, whose `FailingNet` stand-in fails its fetch); the timer advances only through its `TimerTicks` handle (`deliver(n)`, applied on the next pass — a `pump`, an input helper's own pump, or a settle; a delivery made after an input helper waits for a later pass); a driver session moves it by `advance`, which moves the session's clock — the harness's `VirtualClock` — by exactly `ms` inside one settled step, then hands `ms` to `stand::timer_step`, the step the Timer's session carries through `Session::with_time` — whole ticks of `TIMER_TICK_MS` (100), the remainder below one tick carried across calls (250 then 250 → 2 then 3 ticks), `advanced_ms` exactly `ms`, the clock's move (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).
- **5-command discipline (measured):** `bash scripts/agent-run.sh {boot | run {stand|all|session|name} | status | cleanup | logs}` from the repository root (`scripts/agent-run.ps1` passes through to it on Windows). the windowed binary still none), behind escher-telemetry's target allowlist — engine and escher targets scrubbed, every other target's record dropped (bound to obs-plan §3); exercised by the five `telemetry_*` integration files, seven_guis' `host_binary` and `host_log` (no id, no name and no typed text on a host's stderr at `trace` while three hosted calls run, under both builds), a command's stdout — its answer and nothing else, one line of JSON, no ESC byte — by `cli_commands`, the `mcp` role's stdout — protocol lines only — and stderr by `mcp_server` and `mcp_log`, the span line by escher-telemetry's five span unit tests and `stand_act_spans`, and a 10 s boot smoke (exit 124 + `service.name=seven_guis`).
